activity.notes: Representative mid-fourth-century BCE point for Arete's philosophical activity. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy places her activity in the first half of the fourth century BCE but states that the location and duration of her leadership of the Cyrenaic school are unknown; this point does not invent a school tenure.

sources.title: The Cyrenaics — Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.citation_text: SEP identifies Arete as Aristippus' daughter and successor in the Cyrenaic succession, probably active in the first half of the fourth century BCE, while cautioning that where, when, and for how long she headed the school are unknown.
